chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said:

Ali ibn Asbat wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): Regarding the matter of his daughters, that he does not find anyone equal to him. So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) wrote to him: 'I have understood what you mentioned regarding your daughters, and that you do not find anyone equal to you, so do not look [for anyone else] in that matter, may Allah have mercy on you.'

For indeed the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When there comes to you one whose character and religion you are pleased with, then marry him [to her]. If you do not do that, there will be a trial in the earth and great corruption.'

key_terms.الْكَفَاءَة: Compatibility or equality in marriage status

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on finding a spouse equal in status or looking for character and religion?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises Ali ibn Asbat to prioritize moral and religious virtue (*khuluq* and *din*) over rigid social stratification when marrying his daughters, effectively mitigating the potential for *fitnah* caused by excessive status-seeking. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that while compatibility is relevant, it should not become an obstacle to righteous unions, emphasizing that piety is the true measure of worth. The Imam’s guidance underscores the practical implication that preventing social discord is paramount, aligning with the Prophetic tradition cited regarding the consequences of neglecting such marriages.
